generation.explanation: Completing the square turns x² + 6x into a perfect square by thinking geometrically: x² is a square of side x, and 6x is a rectangle we split into two 3x strips placed along two sides of the square. The only thing missing from a full (x + 3) × (x + 3) square is the little 3 × 3 corner, which has area 9. So x² + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)² — use the slider to change x and watch the area model stay balanced, and toggle the corner piece to see why we add 9.
